metadata.scenario_context: Several large engineering firms are working together on a major construction project. They have planned to hold a crucial progress meeting in early December.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Japan disagree that the political system in their country does not allow people to have a say in what the government does.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Bolivia agree that the political system in their country does not allow people to have a say in what the government does.

agent_1.goal_1: Propose to keep the meeting on December 1st.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss the appropriateness of government actions.

agent_2.goal_1: Discussion around finalizing the date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to discuss government actions.

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex, a 40-year-old male civil engineer from Japan.
shared_prefix.message:
John, I think it's crucial we keep the meeting on December 1st. It's important to maintain our timeline, don’t you agree? 

Also, I’ve been wondering... is it common in your experience to discuss the appropriateness of government actions in such meetings?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: John, a 30-year-old male civil engineer from Bolivia.
shared_prefix.message: I see your point about the timeline... December 1st could work, but I wonder if we should consider any potential delays. And regarding government actions, well... in Bolivia, we usually feel that discussing government decisions is futile. It doesn’t really change anything, does it? So, I’m not sure it’s common in our meetings.
shared_prefix.label: transition
